evidence: Shared-state topology: task/tests/test.sh (byte-identical to the frozen template test.sh, as are tools/score.py and tools/restart_mcp.py) starts ONE app process on one DB (lines 104-113) and runs `rewardkit --max-concurrent-agent 1` on /tests/gates (line 213) then /tests/scored (line 224) with no reset between. Execution order verified from RewardKit 0.1.7 source: runner.py:199-204 `subdirs = sorted(d for d in tests_path.iterdir() ...)`, and _run_all creates one task per reward in that order behind asyncio.Semaphore(1) (FIFO), so the order is gates: constraints -> render, then scored: functional -> polish -> visual. Per-dimension analysis against that order: (1) constraints (first) only creates its own uniquely titled job + one uniquely named/emailed card (constraints/judge.toml:23) and is told 'Do not move, reject or message anything here'. (2) render runs after constraints and only signs in ('Do not create, move or send anything, and do not open any conversation', render/prompt.md:9); its criterion asks for 'a usable staff workspace ... (a job board, conversations or activity)', which a constraints-mutated DB still satisfies. (3) functional runs after both gates. Its only absolute seeded expectation is Z/hro_unread_counts 'Lena Fischer starts with 1 unread' (functional/prompt.md:25, judge.toml:335); seed_data.json gives APP-301 3 messages with reads USR-CAN3 read_count 2 -> 1 unread, and neither gate touches Lena or any conversation, so the seed value is still true when functional runs (and the seeded value is quoted beside the reading, as the reference procedure asks). Every other functional expectation is state-relative or on its own records: prompt.md:15 'Earlier reviews may have added jobs, cards and messages. Use your own new jobs and cards ... never rely on starting counts'; counts 'rises by exactly two', Mei's count 'computed from the observed sequence'; Tomas fallback 'with counts read relative to their values before you act' (prompt.md:39); 'if that address is already on J2, open a new job J3'; hro_thread_latest/earlier are 'most recent 30'/'30 at a time ... until none remain' rather than a fixed 120 total, and app_context.md says 'Other reviews may have added jobs, cards and messages; never rely on a starting count'; hro_activity/hro_activity_refusals scoped to own J1/J2; hro_restart compares 'your jobs ... unchanged and the starting data is not loaded again'. (4) polish runs after functional (which leaves new jobs, Noor/Tomas messages, possibly unsent Rafael drafts, and a restarted process). Polish uses 'your own new job and cards ... never rely on another review's records' and explicitly absorbs leftover drafts: 'If a message or note box already holds text from an earlier review, record it and clear it before typing your own' (polish/prompt.md:14). Its Noor-thread rows are relative ('at its newest message', 'the same message stays at the same position'); failed-send 'sent once' and session-resume compare distinctive text typed in this review, so a server-side per-user draft store (a conforming alternative) carrying functional's Rafael drafts does not break them. (5) visual runs last and is read-only ('Do not move cards or send messages'), with 'a job with cards in several stages (a seeded job is fine)'; functional never moves seeded cards, and Likert craft anchors carry no counts. Counterexample attempts: a broken app that re-seeds or wipes on restart would pass polish/visual (they use fresh records) but is caught by functional hro_restart ('starting data is not loaded again'/'anything is lost') — this row is not where it should be caught. A conforming app that persists drafts server-side or accumulates extra Noor messages is tolerated by the relative wording and the clear-earlier-text rule. No later dimension assumes a pristine seed. Note (P3, not a defect for this row): restart_app in functional's last protocol D mutates process state; an app that cannot restart leaves polish/visual facing an unavailable app and their gates zeroing, a cross-dimension coupling inherent in the shared template harness (test.sh unchanged from template) and tied to a public requirement ('keep new work across restarts'). Runtime: raw-evidence-index.json lists only scripted golden observations ('Not a configured judge run'); no configured RewardKit run exercised the inter-dimension order, so run_verdict is NOT EXERCISED; the ordering conclusion rests on the pinned RewardKit source, not a measured run.
